record.final_answer:
No. The report doesn't show that, for two reasons.

**1. It never tested TLS.** The method section says: "Output: the collector over plain TCP. TLS was not enabled in any run." Under "Not covered" it lists TLS and says the maintainers plan to measure it in the Q4 report.

**2. The test lines were much shorter than ours, so the result doesn't fit our load even without TLS.**

| | Report | Our peak (README) |
|---|---|---|
| Lines/s | 180,000 | 50,000 |
| Line size | 200 bytes or less | about 900 bytes on average |
| Bytes/s | 36 MB/s at most | about 45 MB/s |
| CPU | 1 vCPU, at 85% | 1 vCPU reserved |
| Batching | `batch_lines: 500` | `batch_lines: 500` |
| Disk buffer | off | off |
| Transport | plain TCP | TLS (planned) |

Hardware, batching and buffer settings match ours. But per second, our agents move more data than the report's agent did, and it was already at 85% CPU. Lines longer than 200 bytes are also listed under "not covered", so nothing in the report says how it scales to 900-byte lines. Adding TLS encryption would only cost more CPU on top of that.

**What would answer it:** run our own benchmark on one agent VM with 1 vCPU. Replay a sample of our real JSON logs at 50,000 lines/s with `tls: true` in `config/agent.yaml`. Measure CPU and check whether lines back up over a run of at least 30 minutes. Or wait for Marrowlog's Q4 report, but that still won't cover our line size, and the security deadline is the end of next quarter.

I saved a note in memcue that this report can't be used to size agents with TLS, so later sessions don't rely on it.
